facts.title: A Mars Rock With "Leopard Spots" Holds a Potential Sign of Ancient Life
facts.summary: In July 2024, NASA's Perseverance rover found a rock nicknamed "Cheyava Falls" covered in tiny ringed patterns that scientists called "leopard spots." In September 2025, NASA said the rock holds a potential biosignature, a possible sign…

facts.title: A Martian Meteorite Found in Antarctica Once Sparked Claims of Fossil Life
facts.summary: ALH84001 is a 4.5-billion-year-old rock from Mars that landed in Antarctica.

facts.title: A Microwave-Sized Device on Perseverance Made Breathable Oxygen on Mars
facts.summary: An instrument called MOXIE, riding aboard NASA's Perseverance rover, turned the thin Martian air into oxygen.

facts.title: A Mix-Up of English and Metric Units Doomed NASA's Mars Climate Orbiter
facts.summary: NASA's Mars Climate Orbiter was lost in 1999 because some spacecraft commands were sent in English units instead of being converted to metric, according to the review board that investigated the failure.

facts.title: Mars Has Roughly as Much Surface Area as All of Earth's Dry Land
facts.summary: Mars has a diameter only about 53 percent of Earth's, yet its total surface area is roughly equal to all of the dry land on our planet.

facts.title: Mars Is Slowly Tearing Its Moon Phobos Apart
facts.summary: Phobos, the larger of Mars's two moons, is spiraling toward its planet.

facts.title: Mars May Owe Its Red Color to a Water-Rich Mineral, Not Dry Hematite
facts.summary: For decades, scientists thought Mars got its red color from hematite, a dry, rust-like iron mineral.

facts.title: Mars's Two Moons Were Found in 1877 After an Astronomer's Wife Urged Him On
facts.summary: Mars's two moons, Phobos and Deimos, were discovered in August 1877 by American astronomer Asaph Hall, who searched for them in his spare time with the 26-inch refractor at the U.S.

facts.title: Mars's Valles Marineris Canyon Could Stretch From New York to Los Angeles
facts.summary: Valles Marineris, the vast canyon system on Mars, is some 3,000 kilometers (2,000 miles) long.

facts.title: NASA Mission Teams Have Lived on Mars Time, With Days About 40 Minutes Longer
facts.summary: A day on Mars, called a sol, lasts 24 hours, 39 minutes and 35 seconds.

facts.title: NASA's Curiosity Rover Hummed "Happy Birthday" to Itself on Mars Only Once
facts.summary: A popular story says NASA's Curiosity rover sings "Happy Birthday" to itself every year on Mars.

facts.title: NASA's Ingenuity Made the First Powered, Controlled Flight on Another Planet
facts.summary: On April 19, 2021, NASA's Ingenuity helicopter lifted off from the floor of Jezero Crater, making the first powered, controlled flight on another planet.

facts.title: NASA's Opportunity Rover Was Built for 90 Days but Explored Mars for Nearly 15 Years
facts.summary: NASA's Opportunity rover was designed to drive about 1,100 yards (1,006 meters) and to work on Mars for 90 Martian days, or sols.

facts.title: Olympus Mons Is Nearly Two and a Half Times as Tall as Mount Everest
facts.summary: Olympus Mons, a giant volcano on Mars, stands about 21.9 kilometers (13.6 miles, or 72,000 feet) tall.

facts.title: The First Close-Up Image of Mars Was Colored by Hand Like a Paint-by-Numbers
facts.summary: After NASA's Mariner 4 flew past Mars in July 1965, engineers at the Jet Propulsion Laboratory were too impatient to wait for the official processed image.

facts.title: The First Spacecraft to Land Softly on Mars Went Silent After Just 20 Seconds
facts.summary: The Soviet Union's Mars 3 lander became the first spacecraft to make a soft landing on Mars, touching down at 13:50:35 UTC on December 2, 1971.

facts.title: Up to a Third of Mars's Atmosphere Freezes Onto Its Poles Every Winter
facts.summary: Over the course of a Martian year, which lasts 687 Earth days, up to about a third of Mars's thin carbon dioxide atmosphere freezes out onto the polar caps during winter in the north and south.
